key_insight: A matrix-free finite-element Bayesian UQ framework enables scalable 3D photoacoustic tomography by generating posterior samples with only forward and adjoint wave solves.
engineering_relevance: The method supports realistic detector geometries and complex 3D domains, making uncertainty estimates more practical for biomedical imaging and other PDE-constrained inverse problems.
method: Reformulate randomize-then-optimize (RTO) sampling as a matrix-free algorithm.
Use an adjoint discretization that is an exact transpose of the discrete forward operator and consistent with the continuous adjoint.
Study temporal discretization and boundary-condition choices to avoid numerical artifacts in posterior uncertainty.
evidence_signal: The framework is benchmarked against exact posterior statistics, existing Bayesian PAT methods, and NUTS, and demonstrated on a 3D finite-element case with about 2×10^5 unknowns.
watch_item: Posterior quality is sensitive to discretization, so adjoint consistency, time stepping, and artificial boundary conditions must be chosen carefully to avoid biased uncertainty.
paper_title: 3D Uncertainty Quantification for the Photo-Acoustic Tomography
